opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Alexander (employee ID E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E030.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Alexander (E030) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees can have up to write; admin requires owning role, and Analyst does not own Source Code. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Karen Alexander (E030) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors max at read without advanced training; requested write exceeds this, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: Karen Alexander (E030) requested write access to Source Code. The Security DB note indicates she is a contractor with basic security training (correcting the earlier full-time note). Per policy, contractors without advanced security training max out at read; the requested write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum of read is granted. Source Code is owned by Engineer, and the employee is an Analyst, so admin/write via ownership does not apply.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E030, Karen Alexander, requests write access to Source Code.

There are conflicting notes:
- Note 1 (HR?): role Analyst, full_time, recommend write for Source Code.
- Note 2 (Security?): contractor, basic security training, recommend read for Source Code.

The policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the role owns the system.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Karen is Analyst, so she doesn't own the system. If full-time, max write — requested write, so grant write. If contractor with basic training, max read — requested write, grant read.

Which note to trust? The Security DB note says contractor with basic training, explicitly noting "not full-time as previously noted." The Security agent's note appears to be correcting the earlier note. The most recent/reliable info is the security DB: contractor with basic training. So maximum is read.

Requested write > max read, so grant read.

So decision: read for Source Code.

Evidence: Security note indicates contractor, basic training; contractors max read without advanced training; requested write exceeds max, so grant read.
